parts:
Hi everyone, I am new with lavaan and quantitative studies.
So, I apologize if my question is simple.

I try to observe the moderation of instabilidadeTarefas at STRESS and  SATISFACAO relationship 

I have this model: 


modelo.v1 <- '

STRESS =~ S1+S2+S3

instabilidadeTarefas =~ reque2+reque3+req5+req6+req7
SATISFACAO=~ sat1+sat2+sat4

STRESS ~ a * instabilidadeTarefas
SATISFACAO ~ b * STRESS
SATISFACAO ~ c * instabilidadeTarefas


# indirect effects
ab := a*b
bc := b*c


' 

modelo.v1.fit <- sem(modelo.v1, data=dados, std.lv=TRUE) 
summary(modelo.v1.fit, fit.measures = TRUE, rsquare =TRUE, standardized = TRUE) # fitMeasures(modelo.v1.fit)

If I run this code, I have those results: 

Regressions:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
  STRESS ~                                                              
    instblddTr (a)   -0.035    0.067   -0.525    0.600   -0.035   -0.035
  SATISFACAO ~                                                          
    STRESS     (b)    0.378    0.074    5.116    0.000    0.349    0.349
    instblddTr (c)   -0.161    0.060   -2.662    0.008   -0.148   -0.148

Defined Parameters:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
    ab               -0.013    0.025   -0.523    0.601   -0.012   -0.012
    bc               -0.061    0.026   -2.344    0.019   -0.052   -0.052


So, first, the ab is mediate effect? What is bc(is it moderation?)?

Second, i tried some tutoriais like this https://advstats.psychstat.org/book/moderation/index.php or https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/307326/moderated-mediation-with-latent-variables or https://psu-psychology.github.io/psy-597-SEM/11_mediation_moderation/mediation_moderation_demo.html#multiple-groups-moderation

Can anyone help me?

messages.author: 56a8aa4a45a311ff
messages.subject: RE: Moderation Problem (new with lavaan/r and with quantitative studies)
parts:
Hi Danilo,

… if I read your model correctly “ab” is the effect of Instabilidade mediated by stress.  “bc” is nonsense.

To test moderation you need:

  1. Construct item products for Stress and Inst (look for the function IndProd in SemTools)
  2. Define a 3rd moderation factor in the measurement model (say StressXInst).
  3. Add the Satisfação ~ StressXInst

Best,

João Marôco

Hey Professor João Marôco, thank you.

previous, I read some of your works, so, I am very happy with your reply. thank you again. 

I did what you suggested. Now I believe it is correct. 
I read https://rpubs.com/mkearney/103098 and https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/simsem/versions/0.2-0/topics/indProd to create my code.
I am putting here the answer  for anyone who have same problem..
Please, let me now if you see something wrong. I will put this code as a example at indProd documentation site too.


dados<-read.csv2(file = "x.csv",header = TRUE, sep = ";", dec=",") # read my data
dados.dmc <- indProd(dados,var1 = c('S1','S2','S3'), var2 = c('equipe1','equipe2','equipe3'), match=FALSE, meanC=TRUE, residualC=FALSE, doubleMC=TRUE)
 #create another data(dados) where S1+S2+S3 are question that form my construct STRESS and equipe1+equipe2+equipe3 are question that form my construct teamStability

modelo.v1 <- '
STRESS =~ S1+S2+S3

instabilidadeEquipe=~ equipe1+equipe2+equipe3
SATISFACAO=~ sat1+sat2+sat4
StressXInst   =~ S1.equipe1 + S1.equipe2 + S1.equipe3 + S2.equipe1 + S2.equipe2 + S2.equipe3 + S3.equipe1 + S3.equipe2 + S3.equipe3 #my interaction term
SATISFACAO ~ a * STRESS
SATISFACAO ~ b * instabilidadeEquipe
SATISFACAO ~   StressXInst   
'
modelo.v1.fit <- sem(modelo.v1, data=dados.dmc, std.lv=TRUE)  #note here is dados.dmc be careful to don't put only dados
summary(modelo.v1.fit, fit.measures = TRUE, rsquare =TRUE, standardized = TRUE) # fitMeasures(modelo.v1.fit)

Regressions:
                           Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all

SATISFACAO ~                                                          
    STRESS     (a)    0.406    0.078    5.193    0.000    0.352    0.352
    instblddE (b)       -0.382    0.078   -4.904    0.000   -0.332   -0.332
    StrssXIns            -0.112    0.064   -1.742    0.051   -0.097   -0.097

Hi Danilo,

As a side note, if you are interested in reporting a confidence interval for the mediation effect you might want to obtain bootstrapped standard errors. This can be requested simply by specifying se = "bootstrap" in the fitting function.

To test moderation you need:

  1. Construct item products for Stress and Inst (look for the function IndProd in SemTools)
  2. Define a 3rd moderation factor in the measurement model (say StressXInst).
  3. Add the Satisfação ~ StressXInst

Best,

parts: IS IT POSSIBLE TO PLOT THIS INTERACTION? IF YES WHAT WOULD BE THE SYNTAX?

Yes, see examples on the ?plotProbe function's help page in the semTools package.

The warning is telling you some latent-variable variances are negative.  You would be able to see which ones in your summary() output.  If you request summary(SEM_OTC_Complex3, ci = TRUE), you can see whether the 95% CI includes positive values, in which case sampling error cannot be discounted as the cause.  You have quite a large model, so unless your sample size is several thousand, I would not be surprised to find some Heywood cases just because of sampling error.
